title: Everyone sits down and ignores her
note: Replaces the most cluttered composition in the library: two seated figures, sofa, armchair, side table, rug, plant, framed picture, doormat and door. It is now armchair, sofa, bed, wall and floor — nothing else. The armchair and sofa are not in Block A, so their colours are named here, inside the established palette. Re-declared for cool-flat-v2 (the plaster wall) on 2026-09-04; 1 mention(s) of the old room moved to the new hexes and wording. The continuity/likeness attachments are v1 source pictures with lavender walls; the scene text now says what to take from them and what not to.
scene: Interior living space off the same hall, same pale plaster wall and desaturated oak floor. FIVE THINGS ONLY: an armchair, a sofa, the dog bed, the wall and the floor. No side table, no rug, no plant, no framed picture, no lamp, no doormat and no door in frame. The guest sits back in a plain armchair in muted taupe on the right, relaxed, hands in his lap. The guest wears the medium-blue zip-up hoodie, black baseball cap and clear-framed glasses from his likeness reference. He is NOT in a plaid or checked shirt — that was an earlier version of this character and is being replaced everywhere. The handler sits on a plain sofa in muted slate-blue on the left, turned toward him mid-conversation. NEITHER of them is looking at Lucy — both faces are turned toward each other. Lucy lies settled on her cool-grey dog bed — a proper mattress with real thickness, a padded slab about a hand deep with a soft raised edge, not a flat mat on the floor between them, elbows and hips down, head resting level, entirely ignored and entirely fine. No leash. THE ROOM AND GUEST ATTACHMENTS WERE DRAWN IN THE OLD LAVENDER ROOM: match them for the camera, the layout of the room and the guest's face, cap and hoodie only. The wall colour comes from the style block above — warm off-white plaster — and nothing in those attachments overrides it.
mustBeTrue: the picture contains only an armchair, a sofa, the dog bed, the wall and the floor — no table, rug, plant, picture or lamp — and neither the guest nor the handler is looking at Lucy, who lies settled between them.
